subject: Data retention exception - follow-up & proposed schedule
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@finpay.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finpay.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finpay.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery - Data handling questions (recap + ask)

Hi Helen / Tom  

Thanks again for the time today  great conversation on your use case and the compliance envelope. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put a formal exception proposal together: 

Recap (from today)
- Use case: customer support automation + risk alerts (sensitive transactions).
- Primary concern: no persistent storage of PII from user prompts (0-retention for raw query text).
- Secondary: audit/operational logs acceptable but need masking/shortened retention.
- Residency: data must remain in us-east-1.

Asks / next steps for us to finalize a proposal:
1) Can you confirm a) whether FinPay will accept retention of non-content metadata (timestamps, request IDs) for up to 90 days for debugging/audit, and b) whether we need SOC2 attestations / specific cert evidence up front?
2) Please attach your internal retention requirements doc if available (we can align our exception template).

I attached our standard "data_retention_exception_form.pdf"  we can pre-fill based on your answers and return a proposal for engineering/legal review.

Proposed internal owners: Rafael (engineering) to confirm feasibility, Marissa (account lead) for commercial terms, and Neha (security/compliance) on the SOC/attestation path.

Thanks  aiming to get a proposal over by EOD Monday if we have the confirmation.

Best,
Camila
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Attachments:
- data_retention_exception_form.pdf (fillable PDF, 76KB)

From: Helen Park <helen.park@finpay.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finpay.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finpay.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery - Data handling questions (recap + ask)

Hi Camila  

Thanks for the clear recap  that matches our notes. Quick answers below and I attached our internal "finpay_data_retention_requirements.pdf" for specifics.

Answers to your asks:
1) Metadata retention: Yes, FinPay can accept retention of non-content telemetry (request IDs, timestamps, anonymized model usage) for up to 90 days. 0-retention is required for prompt and response content that includes PII.
2) Attestations: We will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a copy of your data handling controls summary before dev access. If you have a SOC report redacted or an SOC summary deck, please share.

Additional constraints:
- Data residency: All processing & ephemeral storage must occur in us-east-1. No cross-region replication for content.
- Auditability: Vendor must provide tamper-evident audit logs for access to any customer data (we accept metadata-only logs for 90 days).

I'll review the exception form and get back with any clarifications, but the three items above are our gating items.

Thanks,
Helen Park
Head of Platform Security | FinPay
helen.park@finpay.com

Attachment:
- finpay_data_retention_requirements.pdf (internal requirements, 210KB)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery - Data handling questions (recap + ask)

Team  forwarding FinPay's reply and requirements (attached). Key asks: 0-retention for PII content, metadata retention up to 90 days, SOC2 evidence, residency in us-east-1.

Can you confirm feasibility and a recommended technical approach we can propose? Rafael, if we can do ephemeral request handling + keep scrubbed metadata for 90 days (and isolate processing to us-east-1), that would solve the engineering side. Neha  what level of SOC evidence can we share pre-sales?

Goal: get a written exception proposal (engineering + legal caveats) back to FinPay by EOD Monday.

Thanks  Camila

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery - Data handling questions (recap + ask)

Camila / Marissa  

We can support FinPay's needs with a scoped exception. High level proposal (engineering):
- Content (prompts/responses): process in-memory and never persist to disk or long-term KV cache. We will enable request-only ephemeral mode for FinPay's account; content will be discarded immediately after response generation.
- Metadata/audit: keep non-content telemetry (request ID, timestamp, model used, token counts) for 90 days in us-east-1. All content fields are redacted/masked before any logs are persisted.
- Logs: operational/debug logs that contain content will be blocked; only masked summaries allowed. Access to logs will be strictly role-based and recorded in tamper-evident audit entries.
- Residency: we will pin FinPay's tenant to us-east-1 and disable cross-region backups for content. Backups for metrics/aggregates can still be multi-region if they do not contain content.

Caveats / work needed:
- We need a legal-approved exception SLA and indemnity language (Marissa / Legal).
- SOC2: we can share a redacted SOC2 Type II report and our security controls summary (pending Neha/legal sign-off).
- Implementation ETA: we can enable ephemeral-content mode and regional pinning in a config change (1 week), and the audit/logging adjustments will require a brief deployment (2 weeks) plus compliance review.

I attached a draft "redwood_exception_proposal_v1.pdf" with these bullets and suggested contract language.

Rafael
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Attachments:
- redwood_exception_proposal_v1.pdf (draft, 48KB)

Camila  

Thanks for the quick turnaround and Rafael for the clear proposal. FinPay is generally comfortable with the approach below and willing to move forward on a pilot subject to: 
1) Receipt of your redacted SOC2 Type II report / controls summary.
2) A short SOW / DocuSign that captures the 0-retention commitment for content, 90-day retention for metadata, residency in us-east-1, and access/audit clauses.

Next steps we propose:
- You send SOC2 evidence & the draft SOW.
- We review internally and return a signed DocuSign (or a couple of redlines).

Please route the SOC2 and SOW to me and Tom. If you can get the SOC2 & the draft SOW over in the next 48 hours we can prioritize legal review on our side.

I attached a short note indicating our internal reviewers (finpay_signed_nextsteps.pdf).

Best,
Helen
